top.line: Our own email connector: one gateway touches Gmail, a twin in a vault, signed lanes, policies at five altitudes.
top.para: Because the usual connectors cannot enforce anything.

in-short.line: The mess; one gateway; the twin; many people one inbox; signed reads; five altitudes; the CRM first; the features.

why.line: Usual connectors: no enforcement, no policies, everything allowed or a click per action, no context.

architecture.line: One gateway holds the token; the mailbox becomes files in a vault; lanes carry proposals, approvals, reads.
architecture.para: An air gap between reading and sending.

flows.line: Connect by tier, receive by watch and history, work together on the twin, send through approval and policy.

signed.line: Proposals, approvals, sends and even reads are signed, ordered on append lanes, not a commit per click.
signed.para: A trail of attention as well as action.

altitudes.line: OAuth grant, token holder, per-agent rights, what an email may be, who approves.
altitudes.para: The fourth altitude is the new one.

features.line: Fifteen features: shared inbox with roles, inbound firewall, signed mail, vault links, approvals anywhere, a calendar twin.
features.para: The brief, not the first slice.

where.line: An AgentiCCells cell, an OAuth app under RiskMandate's Google project, in browser, iPhone CRM and Claude.

google.line: Send is sensitive; read is restricted and needs an assessment if stored on servers; 100 test users before.
google.para: Start in testing with our own inboxes.

plan.line: A build order: our inboxes, lanes and signatures, the email policy, the CRM component, automated sends, the cell.

limits.line: A brief and an architecture, not built; Google's rules to confirm; signed reads record opening, not understanding.

sources.line: Google's Gmail API documentation, integrators' guides, and earlier articles.
